subject: Civil Engineering
title: Rigid Frames: When Joints Don't Rotate
description: Learn Rigid Frames: When Joints Don't Rotate in one minute.

hook.text: A doorframe stays square even when you push on it. The corners are rigid.

buildup.text: Rigid frames have welded or reinforced joints that resist rotation, unlike pin joints.

discovery.text: This stiffness lets the frame resist lateral loads — wind, earthquakes, impact.

twist.text: Most modern buildings are rigid frames — steel or concrete moment-resisting joints.

climax.text: Without rigid frames, skyscrapers would sway too far and crack their walls.

punchline.text: Lock the joints and the whole frame stands stiff.

quiz.question: What makes a rigid frame different from a truss?
options: Rigid frames use cables instead of bars
Rigid frames have joints that resist rotation, not just pin connections
Rigid frames can only be made of wood
